name: fsckprobe
description:
UFS 2.1: 2.11BSD's own fsck(8) RUNNING ON THE 65816, checking a UFS filesystem end to end.  Phase 1's gate arm 3 ran this same source on the live PDP-11 against a volume FGX wrote; this is the other direction -- FGX's own build of it, against a filesystem tools/fgxfs.py made and calls clean.

IT CHECKS A REGULAR FILE, AND THAT IS UPSTREAM'S OWN PATH RATHER THAN A DODGE: setup.c asks "file is not a block or character device; OK" and -y answers it, which is exactly how arm 3 ran fsck on the PDP-11 (no spare partition needed).  A BLOCK DEVICE is not reachable here yet and the reason is recorded rather than incidental -- /dev path resolution is the synthesized CHARDEV registry (_Chardev_LookupSuffix), so `stat("/dev/sd2")' falls through to ProDOS and misses, and stat(2) on a /dev node is one of the three syscalls UFS 1.7d I4 reassigned to the root swap precisely to avoid hooking a tenth path-taking syscall onto the /dev mount.  Measured, not assumed: `stat /dev/null' answers (a registered chardev) and `stat /dev/sd2' says "No such file or directory".

THE COUNTS ARE THE ASSERTION.  fgxfs calls this image `256 blocks (2 used, 248 free)' and fsck answers `2 files, 2 used, 248 free' -- asserted as the WHOLE LINE, because reaching phase 5 proves the walk ran and only the numbers prove it walked the right bytes.  That is where two independent implementations of the format meet, which is the claim goal 2 of the campaign rests on.  The five phase banners are asserted individually because a checker that dies in phase 3 still prints phases 1 and 2.  screen_lacks carries fsck's own complaint vocabulary: on a clean filesystem every one of those words is a failure, and `Can't' is the positive control that the file was actually staged and opened.
